title: Batcher priority-hole investigation and corrective roadmap
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: During a capacity reshuffle on 2026-02-26 we observed recurring micro-silences in the continuous batcher that manifested as intermittent long-tail 95/99 latency spikes for mid-priority traffic. Upstream request rates were within expected ranges and overall throughput remained healthy, but affected customers reported degraded interactive latency for certain chat/assistant flows. This ticket captures the investigation, hypothesized root cause, immediate mitigations, and the roadmap of fixes and validations.
timeline:
2026-02-26 03:12 UTC: First internal alert (service SLO > 95th) triggered for cluster eu-west-1.
2026-02-26 03:18 UTC: Pager notified on-call. Initial triage found elevated p99 for priority class 'standard' while 'realtime' and 'background' classes looked normal.
2026-02-26 03:40 UTC: Deployed emergency config to disable the new dynamic-slot-rebalance heuristic. Latencies partially recovered.
2026-02-26 07:00 UTC: Rollback of allocator heuristic confirmed reduction in spikes but recurrence seen later at lower frequency.
2026-02-27: Deep dive started; correlation with PR #7824 (connection affinity + backpressure refactor) and recent allocator tuning identified.
2026-03-03: Full trace sampling enabled for priority reconciliation path; root cause narrowed to race between slot allocation and in-flight priority reconciliation under bursty microbursts.
2026-03-12: This ticket created to capture postmortem action items and owners.
root_cause: A timing race introduced by two changes: (1) connection-affinity/backpressure refactor (PR #7824) changed ordering so that slot reservations for incoming requests could be returned to the allocator before request priority reconciliation completed; (2) the dynamic-slot-rebalance heuristic reuses recently-freed slots aggressively. Under bursty arrival patterns, the allocator would hand slots to new low-priority requests before the in-flight high- or mid-priority requests could claim them, creating transient 'priority holes' where the visible batching window had insufficient high-priority items to trigger prompt dispatch. The effect is intermittent micro-silences for certain priority classes and amplified tail latency for those classes. The KV-cache warmup behavior made the symptom worse for multi-turn chat flows where earlier tokens retained affinity to specific slots, causing unfair slot preemption patterns.
mitigations_taken: 2026-02-26 04:05 UTC: Increased priority reconciliation timeout to avoid early slot returns (short-term).
2026-02-26 05:12 UTC: Added conservative fairness guard that reserves 10% of live batch slots for 'standard' class to reduce starvation (stop-gap).
action_items: Marco Rivera: Revert the connection-affinity reorder in PR #7824 and create a targeted patch that preserves backpressure semantics while keeping slot allocation atomic - due 2026-03-19
Rina Patel: Implement a per-priority soft-reservation mechanism inside allocator to avoid handouts during reconciliation races; add unit tests - due 2026-03-26
Samir Gupta: Extend trace sampling for priority reconciliation to 10% for 2 weeks and add SLO alerting on per-priority p99 deltas - due 2026-03-16
Infra: Add an allocator simulation harness (synthetic microburst generator) in the CI job to reproduce priority-hole behavior and prevent regressions - owner: Infra Team - due 2026-04-02
Eng Reliability: Make the temporary fairness guard configurable at runtime and remove after validations - owner: Reliability Squad - due 2026-03-22
QA: Create an acceptance test that simulates multi-turn chat affinity + bursty arrivals to validate KV-cache interaction with slot allocator - due 2026-03-30
tests_and_validation: Create allocator unit tests covering: slot handout ordering, reconcile-before-release timing windows, and preferential-reserve edgecases.
Add a performance micro-benchmark that runs in CI nightly to detect p95/p99 regressions per-priority class and flags >10% relative increases.
Run a canary build (runtime-1.24-candidate) with allocator patch against a shadowed traffic replay of last 7 days to verify no reoccurrence.
Post-deploy: 72-hour elevated sampling of priority reconciliation traces and daily report for first 7 days.
Add an automated chaos scenario (network jitter + microbursts) in staging to exercise the allocator under realistic conditions.
notes: Customer reports primarily came from two mid-market customers running interactive assistants that rely on mid-priority 'standard' routing.
SLO blips were most pronounced during cluster autoscaler events when new nodes joined and the allocator rebalanced aggressively.

This failure mode is subtle: overall throughput and average latency metrics can look normal while tail latency for a targeted priority class is impacted. Per-priority metrics are required for future SLOs.
